specAnchors.text: draw and explain energy level diagrams to represent exothermic and endothermic reactions

primer.text: From Exothermic & Endothermic you already know which reactions warm their surroundings and which cool them. This note draws that story as a picture, placing reactants and products on an energy axis so the direction of change can be read at a glance. Two carefully labelled sketches are all the exam asks for.

modules.title: Reading the axes and arrows
modules.opening: An energy level diagram is a map of where the energy sits before and after a reaction. This lesson fixes the axes, the two levels and the arrow that tells you which way the heat flowed.
keyPoints: An energy level diagram sets the energies of reactants and products side by side for comparison.
Energy runs up the y-axis while the x-axis tracks how far the reaction has progressed.
Arrows point downwards for exothermic reactions and upwards for endothermic ones.
The height difference between reactants and products represents the overall enthalpy change.
Reactants sit above products in exothermic reactions and below them in endothermic ones.

low.restatement: The sketch puts energy up the side and the run of the reaction along the bottom. Two lines mark the starting and ending energy, and an arrow between them shows heat leaving or entering.
low.analogy: It is like a thumbnail sketch of a hill walk: the two heights matter, and the arrow between them says whether you climbed or descended.
low.examPointer: Label both axes, both energy levels and the arrow direction whenever you draw or read one.

medium.restatement: The y-axis carries the energy of the reactants and products while the x-axis tracks the progress of the reaction. A downward arrow marks an exothermic change and an upward arrow an endothermic one, with the vertical gap giving the overall enthalpy change.
medium.analogy: Think of a lift journey between two floors: the shaft is the axis, the floors are the energy levels, and the direction of travel is the arrow.
medium.examPointer: Quote both features examiners scan for: labelled axes and a correctly directed arrow between the levels.

modules.title: Drawing the two labelled sketches
modules.opening: The exam rewards two tidy sketches: one with products below reactants, one with products above. This lesson sets out the labels that must never be missing and the negatives that must never creep in.
keyPoints: An exothermic sketch shows reactants high, products low and a downward arrow between them.
An endothermic sketch shows reactants low, products high and an upward arrow between them.
Both sketches need labelled axes, named energy levels and the direction of energy change.
The enthalpy change is negative for the exothermic sketch and positive for the endothermic one.
Energy is given out in exothermic reactions and taken in in endothermic reactions.

low.restatement: Draw the axes first, then two levels: high-to-low with a down arrow for warming reactions, low-to-high with an up arrow for cooling ones. Write the names on every line.
low.analogy: Two sketches are like before-and-after photos on a staircase: the same stairs, but the people stand on different steps.
low.examPointer: Examiners award marks for labels, so annotate axes, levels and arrows before anything else.

medium.restatement: For the exothermic sketch place the reactant level above the product level and mark the change negative with a downward arrow. For the endothermic sketch reverse the placement, mark the change positive and point the arrow upwards.
medium.analogy: It is like drawing water slides in opposite directions: same structure, but one drops and one would need a pump to climb.
medium.examPointer: Pair each sketch with its sign: negative below, positive above, and keep the arrow obeying the same rule.

glossary.definition: A sketch showing the relative energies of reactants and products, with energy on the y-axis and reaction progress on the x-axis.
The difference in height between the reactant and product energy levels.
The starting chemicals, drawn on their own energy level at the left of the diagram.
The finishing chemicals, drawn on their own energy level at the right of the diagram.
The horizontal axis quantity showing how far the reaction has run from start to finish.

workedExample.prompt: a) Describe the energy level diagram of an exothermic reaction. b) Describe the energy level diagram of an endothermic reaction. c) The combustion of methane is exothermic — state where its products sit relative to its reactants and the sign of the enthalpy change.
steps: a) Energy is plotted on the y-axis and reaction progress on the x-axis; the reactant level is drawn high and the product level low, with a downwards arrow between them showing energy given out.
b) The same axes are used, but the reactant level sits low and the product level high, with an upwards arrow showing energy taken in; the enthalpy change is positive.
c) In an exothermic reaction the products sit below the reactants (their energy is lower), so the enthalpy change is negative.
workedExample.finalAnswer: a) Reactants high, products low, downward arrow. b) Reactants low, products high, upward arrow, ΔH positive. c) Products below reactants; ΔH negative.
